We see from the graph that the curves intersect at 

$\,$ $(-3,2)\,$ and $\,(3,2).$ 

Therefore, these are the solutions of the corresponding system.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose we want to solve the following system of equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190078/assets/01eee66dd39797b90503716f097ff604a4f339d8ea0a25ceef9b8ea7a0898ab4.svg)

To solve systems of equations *graphically*, we first draw each of the equations in the same coordinate system. Then, the solution of the system is given by the common points where the lines intersect.

Let's see how this method works for the system above. To plot the functions given by the equations, we first rewrite them by making ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190078/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg) the subject in each equation.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190078/assets/c7778dd2c82032ef68ad8221a990abe1b2bafb4e36a7a0e2640a43856be58c5a.svg) 

Then, we draw the lines in the same coordinate system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190078/assets/47fb02cf8bb4668b24034302fd4265ec5261f4d244cd9d9d599afeffd91d2424.png)

The lines intersect at the point ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190078/assets/d87c68d6226f4bb9ecf52ab576a5ac45c83fbb02c83edd1af04ac235dd518467.svg), which is the solution to our system.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14190078/assets/b3b95135ad9a758f891280b15e8bd6f6165bf9f47a76a1c99280af02dad78911.png)

We can also use the graphical method to solve systems of equations where the corresponding functions are not straight lines. These types of systems are called **nonlinear systems**. Let's consider such an example.
